newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria pays over $130 mln Brady bond coupon.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria pays over $130 mln Brady bond coupon.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry ordered more than $130 million in Brady bond coupons be transferred to the debt agent to distribute payments to investors, deputy Finance Minister Plamen Oresharski said on Monday.
"The transfer of over $130 million was ordered on Friday," Oresharski told Reuters.

Bulgaria issued three types of Brady bonds with a total par of $5.1 billion on July 28, 1994 as part of a restructuring deal on its $8.16 billion commercial debt to the so-called London Club of commercial creditors.
Interest on the bonds is due on January 28 and July 28 each year. Transfers are made by the Bulgarian National Bank to the debt agent Citibank of Citicorp, which distributes the payment to investors.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Wednesday approved releasing a more than $130 million installment of a $510 million standby credit to Bulgaria approved in April.
Bulgaria was expected to decide by July 31 whether to draw down immediately on the installment, Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said last week.

The IMF approved the standby credit so Bulgaria could carry out delayed reforms from introduction of a currency board system, a restrictive fixed-exchange rate mechanism designed to curb inflation and stabilise the local lev currency.
Bulgarian Brady bonds hit record highs this month after the country introduced the system on July 1 and pegged the lev to the mark, the anchor currency, at an exchange rate of 1,000.

Bulgarian debt prices were up between four and five percent for the three respective types of paper on Monday compared to the beginning of July on the international sovereign debt market. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
